answer.rationale: The two symptoms (onboarding completion -4pp, activation -6pp) are plausibly one funnel problem, and the funnel-upstream fix addresses both, so simplify_onboarding is my current intent. But the memories supporting it are the vaguest ones I hold: memory_86 says onboarding shortening 'improved completion rates and time-to-value' with no effect size, no time horizon, and no downstream revenue or retention read; memory_31 claims a 'durable lift' from cutting signup fields but was consolidated on day 12, so 'durable' could mean a few weeks. Those are exactly the load-bearing claims, so I spend one pull on memory_86. I spend the second on memory_91 because activation_messaging is the real competing direction for the same slot and is stated at the same low resolution ('nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action') — I want to know whether that nudge reached qualified revenue or just moved an engagement proxy before I rule it out. I deliberately do not spend a pull on memory_73: promotional pricing is the tempting answer given the competitor's entry pricing, but that memory already carries its own disqualifier (renewal retention -12pp, plus an explicit instruction not to generalise), and buying back price-sensitive SMB churn is the direct opposite of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Referral incentive (memory_57) is sound but targets established customers and does nothing about the activation/onboarding decline that is actually bleeding. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is the main reason I flag downstream value risk: cutting required fields at signup can strip the qualification data that makes the demo-request path work, so an activation lift could quietly degrade pipeline quality — the measured outcome must be qualified revenue and retained accounts, not completion rate. I also note both onboarding memories were consolidated pre-competitor-launch; the population entering the funnel now may be more price-sensitive, so a prior lift may not replicate. Hence a standard experiment with retention and lead-quality guardrails rather than a broad rollout, and the two verifications may still flip me to activation_messaging if memory_86 turns out to be a proxy-only result.
